title: Tidal Will Delete 29 Million AI-Generated Songs in First Big Streaming Ban
yt_title: Tidal Deletes 29 Million AI Songs: First Big Streamer to Ban AI Music
yt_description:
Tidal is done with AI slop. Starting December 9, the music streamer will delete fully AI-generated tracks, around 29 million songs, and reject about 80,000 new AI uploads every day. AI-assisted music made by humans can stay. Here is what changed, why, and how Spotify, Deezer, YouTube Music and Bandcamp compare.

script: Welcome to IT News, AI News! Today, a music streamer just hit the delete button on robot songs. Millions of them! The streamer is Tidal. On November twenty fourth it announced a full ban on music made entirely by AI. Starting December ninth, Tidal will begin deleting fully AI generated tracks from its catalogue. How many? About twenty nine million songs. That is a very, very big playlist going straight to the bin. And the flood is real. Tidal says more than forty three percent of tracks delivered in the last ninety days were AI made. New uploads are blocked too. Tidal expects to reject around eighty thousand AI tracks every single day. Here is the funny part. Ninety six percent of the AI labelled tracks had zero streams in three months. Nobody was listening! Back in June, Tidal only cut royalties for AI songs and stuck an AI badge on them. It says that was not enough. Platform lead Robert Anderson put it simply: something more drastic needs to be done. To spot the robots, Tidal uses detection from Ircam Amplify, checking the audio and the track details. But AI assisted music is still welcome. If a human makes the song and AI just helps, it can stay. And if an artist thinks they were flagged by mistake, they can appeal through Tidal support. Tidal says it is the first big streaming service to do this. Bandcamp banned AI music back in January. Spotify, YouTube Music and Deezer mostly label AI songs or push them out of recommendations, but keep them online. So, will the other giants follow Tidal, or keep the robots on the playlist?
